ai.literal: Women of feminine nature all with eyes in common will consume; I will not approach, O playboy, your chest.
ai.translation: All women feast upon your chest with their eyes as if it were common property; therefore, O playboy, I will not embrace your chest.
ai.modern: பெண் தன்மை உடையவர்கள் எல்லாரும் உன்னுடைய மார்பைத் தங்கள் கண்களால் பொதுவானதாக நுகர்கிறார்கள்; பரத்தனே, அதனால் நான் உன்னுடைய மார்பைத் தழுவ மாட்டேன்.
ai.explanation: In this couplet, the heroine expresses her feigned anger towards her lover by calling him a playboy ('paratta'). She accuses him of being so attractive that all women feast upon his chest with their eyes, making his chest a 'common property' shared by everyone. Because his chest is thus 'consumed' by the gaze of other women, she proudly refuses to touch or embrace it, claiming she does not want something that is shared publicly. This playful jealousy highlights the intimacy and the subtle, teasing conflicts between lovers.

ai.literal: While we were sulking, he sneezed, knowing that I would say 'live long!' to him.
ai.translation: While we were in a feigned tiff, he sneezed, knowing that I would be forced to break my silence and wish him a long life.
ai.modern: நாங்கள் ஊடல் கொண்டு இருந்தபோது, நான் அவருக்கு 'நீடூழி வாழ்க' என்று வாழ்த்துவேன் என்பதை அறிந்து அவர் தும்மினார்.
ai.explanation: The heroine is feigning anger and maintaining a stubborn silence. To break this silence, the husband deliberately sneezes. According to ancient custom, when someone sneezes, their partner must immediately bless them by saying 'Live long!' (நீடுவாழ்க). The heroine realizes his clever trick: he sneezed on purpose, knowing that her love and duty would compel her to break her silent protest just to offer him the customary blessing.

ai.literal: Even if I wear a branch flower, she will get angry, saying, 'You wore it to show to another woman!'
ai.translation: Even if I wear a flower plucked from a tree branch, she will get angry and say, 'You wore this only to show it off to some other woman!'
ai.modern: மரக்கிளையில் மலர்ந்த பூவை நான் சூடிக்கொண்டாலும், 'வேறொரு பெண்ணுக்குக் காட்டுவதற்காகவே இதனைச் சூடினீர்' என்று கூறி அவள் என்னோடு ஊடல் கொள்வாள்.
ai.explanation: In this couplet from the chapter on the subtleties of lovers' tiffs, the hero laments his beloved's playful jealousy. Even an innocent act like wearing a flower from a tree branch (கோட்டுப் பூ) triggers her suspicion. She immediately accuses him of wearing it to show off (காட்டிய) to another woman (ஒருத்தியை). The word 'காயும்' captures her swift, feigned anger, which is a characteristic part of their intimate lovers' tiff.

ai.literal: I said, 'We love more than anyone,' alas! She sulked, saying, 'More than whom? More than whom?'
ai.translation: When I said, 'I love you more than anyone else,' she immediately sulked, demanding, 'More than whom? More than whom?'
ai.modern: நான் 'உன்னை எல்லாரையும் விட அதிகமாகக் காதலிக்கிறேன்' என்று சொன்னேன்; உடனே அவள் 'யாரை விட? யாரை விட?' என்று கேட்டு ஊடினாள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet portrays a delicate moment of feigned anger (pulavi) between lovers. The hero attempts to express the depth of his affection by saying he loves her more than anyone else. However, the heroine quickly seizes upon his words and turns them into a cause for suspicion. By asking 'More than whom? More than whom?', she playfully implies that he must have loved other women to make such a comparison. The repetition of 'yāriṉum' highlights her swift, jealous wit and the charming complexity of her sulking.

ai.literal: In this birth we will not separate, as soon as I said, her eyes filled with tears.
ai.translation: When I said, 'We will not part in this life,' her eyes immediately filled with tears, fearing that we might part in the next.
ai.modern: "இப்பிறப்பில் நாம் பிரிய மாட்டோம்" என்று நான் சொன்ன உடனே, அவள் கண்கள் நிறையக் கண்ணீர் கொண்டாள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet illustrates a delicate nuance of a lovers' tiff. When the hero reassures his beloved by saying they will not separate in this life, she immediately focuses on what he did not say. She interprets his words to mean that they might separate in future births, which fills her with sorrow. Consequently, her eyes instantly well up with tears, showing her longing for an eternal, uninterrupted union across all births.

ai.literal: "I thought [of you]," I said; "then, what did you forget [about me]?" saying, me she did not embrace, she sulked.
ai.translation: I told her, "I was thinking of you." Immediately she asked, "What did you forget about me that you had to think of me?" and, refusing to embrace me, she began to sulk.
ai.modern: "நான் உன்னை நினைத்தேன்" என்று கூறினேன்; "அப்படியானால் என்னை எப்போது மறந்தீர்கள்?" என்று கேட்டு, என்னைத் தழுவாமல் அவள் ஊடல் கொண்டாள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet portrays a delicate and witty moment of a lovers' tiff. When the hero tries to show his affection by saying he was thinking of her, the heroine cleverly turns it against him. She reasons that one only needs to think of someone if they had forgotten them first, and asks what he had forgotten. Refusing his embrace, she playfully sulks, showing how even loving words can be turned into a reason for a sweet argument.

ai.literal: She blessed me; I sneezed; immediately, breaking down, she wept, saying, 'Thinking of whom did you sneeze?'
ai.translation: She blessed me when I sneezed, but immediately changed her mood and wept, asking, 'Thinking of which other woman did you sneeze?'
ai.modern: நான் தும்மியபோது அவள் என்னை வாழ்த்தினாள்; ஆனால் உடனே தன் மனநிலையை மாற்றிக்கொண்டு, 'யாரை நினைத்துக் கொண்டு தும்மினீர்?' என்று கேட்டு அழுதுவிட்டாள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet portrays a playful lover's tiff based on a traditional belief. In Tamil culture, a sneeze is believed to occur when someone is thinking of you, and it is customary to bless the person who sneezes. When the hero sneezes, the heroine instinctively blesses him out of love. However, she immediately realizes the implication of the sneeze: someone else must have been thinking of him. Suspecting that another woman was remembering her lover, she breaks down in tears and demands to know who that woman is.

To avoid making his wife jealous, the husband tries to suppress his sneeze. However, the wife notices this and interprets his action as an attempt to hide the sneeze, accusing him of trying to conceal the fact that another woman (referred to as 'your people') is thinking of him.

ai.literal: Even if he appeases her, she will grow angry, saying, 'To other women also, you behave with this same nature!'
ai.translation: Even when he tries to appease and reassure her of his love, she grows angry, saying, 'This is exactly how you must behave with other women too!'
ai.modern: தலைவன் தன் அன்பை வெளிப்படுத்தித் தலைவியைச் சமாதானப்படுத்த முயன்றாலும், 'மற்றப் பெண்களிடமும் நீங்கள் இப்படித்தான் நடந்து கொள்வீர்கள்' என்று கூறி அவள் கோபப்படுகிறாள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet portrays a delicate moment of lovers' tiff where the heroine's intense love manifests as playful jealousy. When the hero tries to comfort and appease her, she becomes angry instead of being pacified. She suspects his gentle, loving behavior is not unique to her, accusing him of using the same charming manners to win over other women. Her anger is a reflection of her deep desire for his exclusive affection, turning even his attempts at reconciliation into a source of sweet dispute.

ai.literal: Even if I look at her having been thinking of her, she gets angry saying, 'With that much intensity, whom did you think of and look at me?'
ai.translation: Even when I gaze at her after thinking of her with deep affection, she gets angry and demands, 'Whom were you thinking of, to look at me with such intense passion?'
ai.modern: நான் அவளையே நினைத்துக் கொண்டு அவளைப் பார்த்தாலும், 'நீர் யாரை நினைத்துக் கொண்டு என்னை இப்படிப் பார்க்கிறீர்?' என்று சொல்லி அவள் கோபித்துக் கொள்கிறாள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet depicts a subtle lover's tiff where the heroine finds a reason to be angry even in her lover's affectionate gaze. The hero has been thinking of her constantly, and when he looks at her with that deep, lingering love, she misinterprets his intense look. She asks him, 'Whom were you thinking of just now, that you look at me with such a look?' The word 'அனைத்து' refers to the intensity or manner of his gaze, and 'உள்ளி' means remembering or thinking of someone. Her feigned anger shows the playful, delicate nature of their love.
